About / Michal WochnaPROFILE

IT & BUSINESS SYSTEMS MANAGER

Hi, I’m
Michal Wochna_

I look after IT and business systems at Advanced Safety in Castlebar.

Stock, orders, warehouse processes, websites, vending machines and the data moving between them — that’s where I spend most of my working day.

I work with the people using those systems, figure out what’s getting in their way, and help sort it out. Sometimes that means changing a process. Sometimes it means building a tool that doesn’t exist yet.

Work / Advanced Safety

01

A broad job.
A lot of connected parts.

I’ve been at Advanced Safety for over fifteen years. My role has grown across IT, eCommerce, business systems and process improvement, working with sales, customer service, the warehouse and production.

A website problem can start with product data. An ERP issue can turn out to be a warehouse process. A lot of the job is following those connections until the problem makes sense.

01

ERP, warehouse systems & data

Intact iQ, warehouse workflows, stock and product data. I’ve worked on ERP and WMS implementation, reporting, and checks that catch bad data before it causes trouble elsewhere.

02

eCommerce & internal tools

Websites, product information, ordering and garment-fitting workflows. I build small applications, integrations and automations where the existing tools leave a gap.

03

Vending & replenishment

Vending systems, live dashboards, usage reporting and Kanban workflows. This work brings together the machines, the software and what people need on site.

04

IT, security & everyday support

Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, infrastructure and support for colleagues. My cybersecurity study also feeds into how I approach access, configuration and risk.

Some days I’m configuring a system. Other days I’m writing a tool, checking a report or helping someone work through a problem. I enjoy having that range.

Backstory / Before the job title

03

It started with
a Commodore 16.

I was born in Poland in 1980. My dad brought home a Commodore 16, and we’d go to the giełda komputerowa together, looking for parts and cassettes. A C64 came next, then an Amiga 500.

Later it was 286s, 486s and Pentiums. Building PCs, taking them apart, working out memory settings and editing CONFIG.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT. I wanted to understand what was going on inside.

I also taught people how to use computers, from switching one on to Windows and the TAG word processor. I went on to study geography and train as a teacher. Explaining things and helping people get comfortable with a system is still a part of the work I enjoy.

C16 → C64 → AMIGA 500 → PC

Outside work

04

There’s usually
a computer involved.

I run a Proxmox homelab, tinker with my home network and still use a working Commodore 64. I also play on Xbox — usually something long, like Cyberpunk or Fallout.

I run, cycle and swim, too. I’m still fairly new to running, and I like having something to work towards.

I have two boys. Giving them their first computers and games, the same way my dad did for me, is something I’m proud of.
